svg.text: Action parameters and asset variables — one model, three questions
The action does not own its params. The VARIABLE is the storage; the action's DTO is a lens onto it.
1 · AUTHORED — the asset declares variables
Each variable has a Role and, when Role = State, a Scope. Those two answer "where does it live" and "who shares it".
MoveToParams · Role = Input
Destination : Vector3
Speed : float
DefaultValueJson → applied once at
behaviour assignment (ParseParams)
CursorState · Role = State
Index : int
Elapsed : float
Scope = Node | Behavior | Entity
no default — provisioned, then owned
⭐ Role answers ONE question, Scope answers a DIFFERENT one
Role → which tier the bytes live in. Input → the 100-byte inline region. State → the partition tier.
Scope → who else sees the same bytes. It is meaningless for Input, because Input is per-behaviour by construction.
This is why they are two fields and not one enum — they are orthogonal, not a hierarchy.
2 · BOUND — a call site picks variables. It does not declare them.
A BTree node, or an HSM state-slot, names up to two variables. Whole-variable binding only — never a field of one.
BTree — today
ExpressionTargetField
→ the Input variable (params)
WorkingStateTargetField
→ the State variable (working state)
Both optional. When only one is set it
serves both roles (the legacy shape).
HSM — the gap
A state has FOUR call sites:
OnEntry · OnExit · Activity · Timer
a transition has TWO: guard · effect
⛔ StateNode has NO target field.
It stores four action-name strings and
nothing to bind them to. (DEBT-BF-04)
⭐ What unification means, concretely
The carrier stops being "a field on a node" and becomes
a binding keyed by a call site:
BTree : (AssetId, NodeVisualId)
HSM : (AssetId, StableId, SlotKind)
⭐ Same tuple, one term wider. Everything downstream
— offsets, keys, thunks, scope — is unchanged.
3 · RUNTIME — two tiers, and the Role picked which
Role = Input → BrainBlackboard.BehaviorParameters
fixed byte[100], bin-packed in declaration order
Speed
Destination
…free…
The action's DTO is Unsafe.As over the slice at the packed offset.
⇒ a write through the ref IS a write to the variable. No copy-back step.
Two nodes binding the same variable get the same offset ⇒ true zero-copy sharing.
Role = State → the partitioned working-state tier
Blackboard1024+; slots provisioned at behaviour assignment, detached on switch
⭐ Scope decides the slot key — i.e. who shares the bytes
Node FNV(assetId ++ nodeVisualId) → private to this call site
Behavior FNV(assetId ++ variableId) → every node in the asset that binds it
Entity FNV(variableId) → survives a behaviour switch
⭐ Sharing is not a flag. It is what the key omits — drop the node, share across nodes.
The registry key ties all three bands together — and it is the thing HSM must reach
"{MethodFqn}@{paramOffset}@{slotKey}"
↑ band 1 chose the offset · band 2 chose the call site · band 3's scope chose the slotKey
⭐ The generator emits one thunk per distinct key, with the offset and slot key baked in as constants. The kernel never
computes an offset — it looks up a key. That is why the same mechanism serves BTree and HSM: only the key's middle term differs.
⛔ HSM's gap is exactly this: its thunks are emitted from source attributes, so the editor cannot request a key that no attribute already declared.
